description.value: A secondary analysis examined whether peak methamphetamine-induced craving during an intravenous methamphetamine challenge was associated with neural reactivity to methamphetamine cues during fMRI in individuals with methamphetamine use disorder.

spans.text: the primary objective of this secondary analysis was to integrate human laboratory and neuroimaging methodologies to assess if methamphetamine-induced craving responses were associated with neural responses to methamphetamine cues.

description.value: Non-treatment-seeking individuals with methamphetamine use disorder completed two 5-day inpatient protocols, with placebo data used for this secondary analysis; participants were scanned on Day 3 and completed an intravenous methamphetamine challenge on Day 4.

spans.text: Sixteen medically eligible, non–treatment-seeking individuals with current methamphetamine abuse or dependence completed two, 5-day inpatient protocols investigating the effects of a medication (naltrexone) on subjective response to methamphetamine administration ( Ray et al., 2015 ) and on neural substrates of methamphetamine cue-reactivity ( Courtney et al., 2016 ). Data collected while participants were under placebo were used for the present study
